nodes.title: SG-7.3 · Implement the execution runner in worker/internal
nodes.body:
Context: backend/worker has config, lock (lock.Acquire/ErrLocked) and store (store.Store, Execution, Status) packages but no runner. Desired behavior: a runner package that locks, runs an agent in an isolated worktree under a context timeout, retries up to the configured limit, stops when budget is exceeded and blocks at the approval gate before publishing unless auto-publish is on. Expected result: Runner.Run drives one execution to COMPLETED, AWAITING_APPROVAL or FAILED. Why: the worker must never corrupt production and must run one execution per World.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the lock file exists, when Run is called, then it returns an error satisfying errors.Is(err, lock.ErrLocked) and neither the worktree nor the agent is touched
- Given an agent that blocks, when the timeout elapses, then Run returns context.DeadlineExceeded and the execution is FAILED
- Given an agent failing twice then succeeding and MaxRetries 2, when Run is called, then the agent runs 3 times and the execution is not FAILED
- Given the accumulated cost exceeds MaxBudget, when an attempt finishes, then Run stops retrying and returns ErrBudgetExceeded
- Given AutoPublish is false and the agent succeeds, then the status is AWAITING_APPROVAL and Publish is not called; when true, Publish is called and status is COMPLETED


## Scope
- In scope: new package backend/worker/internal/runner
- Out of scope: real git worktree and Claude provider implementations
- Out of scope: admin approve endpoint
- Out of scope: startup recovery
- Preserve: lock, store and config package APIs


## Technical constraints
- Go 1.22, standard library only plus existing packages
- Agent, Worktrees and Publisher are interfaces so tests use fakes


## Definition of done
- All acceptance criteria are met by runner package code


## Non-functional requirements
- No shell interpolation of any prompt text


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Run takes the per-World lock, runs the agent in an isolated worktree under a timeout
nodes.body:
Context: lock.Acquire returns an error wrapping lock.ErrLocked when the lock file exists. Desired behavior: Run acquires cfg.LockPath first, persists a RUNNING execution, creates a worktree under WorkRoot/<id>, runs the agent with context.WithTimeout(cfg.Timeout), then removes the worktree on completion or failure. Expected result: a held lock yields a locked error with no side effects. Why: one execution per World and isolation from production files.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the lock file already exists, when Run is called, then the returned error satisfies errors.Is(err, lock.ErrLocked) and Worktrees.Create is never called
- Given a successful agent, when Run returns, then the lock file no longer exists and Worktrees.Remove was called with the worktree directory
- Given an agent that waits for ctx.Done and Timeout 20ms, when Run is called, then the error satisfies errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) and the stored status is FAILED


## Scope
- In scope: runner.go with types, New and Run
- Out of scope: retry and budget
- Out of scope: approval gate
- Preserve: lock.Acquire semantics


## Technical constraints
- Worktree directory is filepath.Join(cfg.WorkRoot, id)


## Definition of done
- Run locks, isolates and times out as specified


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Run retries up to the configured limit and stops when the budget is exceeded
nodes.body:
Context: config exposes MaxRetries and MaxBudget. Desired behavior: Run attempts the agent up to MaxRetries+1 times, recording Execution.Attempt, summing cost returned by each attempt, and stopping with ErrBudgetExceeded as soon as total cost exceeds MaxBudget. Expected result: bounded, budget-safe agent runs. Why: avoid runaway cost and endless loops.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given an agent failing twice then succeeding and MaxRetries 2, when Run is called, then the agent is called 3 times and the stored Attempt is 3
- Given an agent that always fails and MaxRetries 1, when Run is called, then the agent is called 2 times, the status is FAILED and Error contains the agent error
- Given each attempt costs 3.0 and MaxBudget 5.0, when the second attempt finishes, then Run returns an error satisfying errors.Is(err, ErrBudgetExceeded) and no third attempt runs


## Scope
- In scope: retry loop in Run's execute step
- In scope: ErrBudgetExceeded
- Out of scope: backoff delays
- Preserve: R1 lock and timeout behavior


## Technical constraints
- Budget check runs after each attempt, including a failed one


## Dependencies
- R1


## Definition of done
- Retry and budget limits enforced


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Run blocks at the approval gate before publishing unless auto-publish is on
nodes.body:
Context: store.StatusAwaitingApproval and Config.AutoPublish exist. Desired behavior: on agent success, if AutoPublish is false Run saves status AWAITING_APPROVAL, keeps the worktree and does not call Publisher.Publish; if true it calls Publish and saves COMPLETED. Expected result: supervised publishing by default. Why: human approval of first releases.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given AutoPublish false and a successful agent, when Run is called, then the returned execution status is AWAITING_APPROVAL, the stored status matches, Publish is never called and Worktrees.Remove is not called
- Given AutoPublish true and a successful agent, when Run is called, then Publish is called once with the worktree directory and status is COMPLETED
- Given AutoPublish true and Publish returns an error, when Run is called, then the status is FAILED and the error is returned


## Scope
- In scope: gate logic in Run's finish step
- Out of scope: Approve call that publishes later
- Preserve: R1 and R2 behavior


## Dependencies
- R1


## Definition of done
- Gate behaves per criteria


## Clarifying questions
- None

acceptance_criteria: Run returns a lock.ErrLocked-wrapping error when the lock is held
Run applies cfg.Timeout via context.WithTimeout

steps.symbol: new: interfaces Agent, Worktrees, Publisher and type Config
steps.action: Create package runner importing context, errors, fmt, path/filepath, time, github.com/worldseed/storyforge/worker/internal/lock and .../internal/store. Declare Agent, Worktrees, Publisher interfaces and Config struct.
steps.expected: Package compiles with the four declarations

steps.action: Declare Runner holding cfg Config, st *store.Store, agent Agent, trees Worktrees, pub Publisher, now func() time.Time, and New(cfg, st, agent, trees, pub, now) *Runner assigning each field.
steps.code: func New(cfg Config, st *store.Store, a Agent, t Worktrees, p Publisher, now func() time.Time) *Runner

steps.action: Implement Run(ctx, id, roundID string) (store.Execution, error): (1) l, err := lock.Acquire(cfg.LockPath); on err return store.Execution{}, fmt.Errorf("runner: %w", err); defer l.Release(). (2) build e := store.Execution{ID:id, RoundID:roundID, Status:store.StatusRunning, CreatedAt:r.now(), UpdatedAt:r.now()} and st.Save(e), returning the error. (3) dir := filepath.Join(cfg.WorkRoot, id); call trees.Create(ctx, dir), on error fail. (4) tctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, cfg.Timeout); defer cancel(). (5) e.Attempt = 1; _, err = agent.Run(tctx, dir). (6) on err set e.Status=StatusFailed, e.Error=err.Error(), UpdatedAt, Save, call trees.Remove(ctx, dir), return e, err. (7) on success set e.Status=StatusCompleted, Save, trees.Remove(ctx, dir), return e, nil.
steps.expected: Held lock returns lock.ErrLocked; timeout yields FAILED with DeadlineExceeded

nodes.summary: Replace the single agent call with a bounded retry loop and ErrBudgetExceeded
nodes.description: Edit runner.go so step 5 loops attempts 1..MaxRetries+1, accumulates cost and stops on budget overrun.
acceptance_criteria: Agent is retried up to MaxRetries times
Total cost above MaxBudget returns ErrBudgetExceeded
technical_constraints: Depends on Act: Create the runner package having been done

steps.action: Declare an exported sentinel error for budget overrun.

steps.lines: the single `e.Attempt = 1; _, err = agent.Run(tctx, dir)` statement in Run
steps.action: Replace with a loop: var total float64; for attempt := 1; attempt <= r.cfg.MaxRetries+1; attempt++ { e.Attempt = attempt; cost, aerr := r.agent.Run(tctx, dir); total += cost; if total > r.cfg.MaxBudget { err = fmt.Errorf("%w: spent %.2f of %.2f", ErrBudgetExceeded, total, r.cfg.MaxBudget); break }; err = aerr; if aerr == nil || tctx.Err() != nil { break } }. Existing failure/success handling then runs on err.
steps.code:
before: e.Attempt = 1; _, err = agent.Run(tctx, dir)
after: loop as described
steps.expected: Retries bounded; budget error wraps ErrBudgetExceeded and stored Attempt equals attempts made
